albums_help: An album is what a photo frame or a screensaver shows: the widget names it by its ID. The widget also decides which days of the album it shows: the last days, a period, or this day some years ago.
col_id_tooltip: Letters, digits, - and _; the widgets name the album by it
col_location_tooltip: ioBroker files: like 0_userdata.0/photos. Folder of the server: like /mnt/nas/photos. Immich: name of the album, empty for the whole library. Google Photos: name of a source chosen in the app, empty for the selection of Google
immich_help: Immich is a photo server of your own; the Immich app uploads the photos of the phone to it. ioBroker can run Immich in Docker on this host, or use a server that runs elsewhere: then create an API key in Immich under Account settings, API keys; reading is enough (asset.read, asset.view, asset.download, album.read). The key stays in ioBroker: the browser only gets reduced copies.
maxEdge: Largest edge of a reduced picture
maxEdge_help: Each frame gets the next larger size above its own; this is the limit. Larger costs memory on the tablet.
cacheSizeMb_help: Reduced copies in the files of the instance; those used longest ago are dropped first
rescanMinutes_help: Folders of the ioBroker files report new pictures at once; folders of the server and Immich are read at this interval
google_help: Shows pictures of your Google Photos library. ioBroker becomes a device in Google Photos, like a photo frame: in the Google Photos app you choose which albums, people or pets it shows. Google leaves out screenshots, documents and very personal pictures by itself. Then add an album with the source Google Photos on the first tab: in its folder field the name of a source chosen in the app, or nothing for the selection of Google.
google_permissions: When you connect, Google asks you to allow ioBroker two things: to see your name and profile picture, so that this page shows which Google Account is connected, and to see the photos you choose for this device in the Google Photos app. ioBroker does not see the rest of your Google Photos library and cannot change or delete anything there. Copies of the photos are kept for at most 60 minutes. "Disconnect" removes the device from Google Photos, withdraws the permission and deletes the copies.
google_device_name_help: The name of this device in the Google Photos app, where you choose what it shows. Empty: ioBroker and the name of the host. Used when connecting.
google_disconnect_confirm: Remove ioBroker from Google Photos? The permission is withdrawn and the copies of the photos are deleted. The albums of Google Photos stay empty until you connect again.
google_status_code: Open %s on a phone or computer (or scan the QR code) and enter this code:
google_status_sources: Connected. Now choose in Google Photos what ioBroker shows:
google_status_expired: The sign-in at Google ran out or was revoked. Connect again.
google_status_gone: ioBroker was removed in Google Photos. Connect again.
google_status_denied: The sign-in was not completed. Connect again.
google_status_not_allowed: Google does not let ioBroker into Google Photos yet: the Ambient API is only open to partners of Google Photos. Connect again once Google has granted access.
immich_docker: Run Immich in Docker on this host
immich_docker_help: ioBroker starts the containers and connects itself; about 2 GB to download and 2 GB of memory
immich_location_help: On a disk with enough space; Immich keeps the photos, their thumbnails and a nightly backup of its database (backups/) there. Move the content yourself before choosing another folder.
immich_location_error: Choose the folder for the photos (a full path)
immich_email_help: On a new Immich ioBroker creates this account (administrator); log in with it in the app and in the browser
immich_password_help: stored encrypted; ioBroker signs in only to create its API key
immich_bind_help: 0.0.0.0: from all devices of the network, so the app on the phone can upload
immich_ml_help: One more container; needs 1–2 GB of memory more. The photo frame does not need it.
immich_auto_update_help: Newer versions of Immich 3 are pulled when the instance starts
immich_stop_help: Otherwise Immich keeps running and the phones keep uploading
immich_status_no_folder: Choose the folder for the photos and save: the containers start then.
immich_status_folder_missing: The folder %s does not exist, and ioBroker may not create it. Create it on the host, then restart the instance:
immich_folder_will_create: The folder does not exist yet: ioBroker creates it when the instance starts.
immich_folder_not_folder: A file is in the way: this path is not a folder.
immich_folder_cannot_create: The folder does not exist, and ioBroker may not create it (no write permission in %s). Create it on the host:
immich_folder_cannot_check: ioBroker may not look into a folder above, so it cannot tell whether this folder exists. If it does not, create it on the host:
immich_status_starting: Immich is starting. On the first start Docker downloads about 2 GB; that can take a few minutes.
immich_status_no_account: Immich runs. Enter the e-mail and the password of the Immich account and save: on a new Immich ioBroker creates the account, then it connects itself.
immich_status_login_failed: Immich did not accept the e-mail or the password. ioBroker only creates the account on a new Immich; if there is an account already, enter its e-mail and password.
immich_status_app: Server address for the Immich app: %s
immich_status_local_only: Immich only listens on this host: the app on the phone cannot reach it. Choose 0.0.0.0 or an IP of the host.
